pages.text: Heat is one of your greatest challenges. When your body temperature exceeds your comfortable range, you'll begin suffering from hyperthermia, which can quickly become deadly if left unmanaged.
pages.title: Overheating

pages.text: As you overheat, you'll experience increasingly severe effects:$(br)$(li)Confusion effect$(li)Damage $(li)Tunnel Vision

Several factors increase your temperature:$(li)Solar radiation - direct sunlight$(li)Nearby heat blocks - forges, fires, lava$(li)Hot fluids - molten metal, lava$(li)High ambient temperature - desert biomes$(li)Low wind - still air prevents cooling$(li)High humidity - reduces evaporation
pages.title: What Causes Heat

pages.text: $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#shade)$(l)Seek Shade$()$(br)Shade actually works in Thermia. Hiding under a block isn't enough, you need to be out of the sun's line of sight. Trees, caves, overhangs all cast real shadows.$(br2)$(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#wetness)$(l)Get Wet$()$()$(br)Water is your best friend. Jump in a river or stand out in the rain and watch your temperature drop. Your body sweats too, so keep your water full or you'll dry out and overheat faster.
pages.title: Staying Cool

pages.text: $(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#wind)$(l)Find Wind$()$()$(br)Wind enhances evaporative cooling dramatically. Exposed hilltops and open areas have stronger winds.$(br2)$(l)Avoid Heat Sources$()$(br)Stay away from forges, fires, and lava. Even proximity radiates significant heat. If you must work with heat, do so quickly or palce sources behind walls.

$(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#insulation)$(l)Insulation$()$(br)Insulation can help or hinder cooling as it can slow transfer with the environment, Radiative protection can also help block sources like fire, lava or the sun.$(br2)$(l)Time Your Activities$()$(br)Work during dawn, dusk, or night when solar radiation is minimal. Rest in shade during peak sun hours.

$(l:tfc:thermia/mechanics#sweat)$(l)Sweating$()$(br)Your body automatically sweats when hot, if you have sufficient hydration. This converts thirst into cooling$(br2)$(l)Wet Bulb Temperature$(): In very humid environments, sweating becomes less effective. Seek wind or shade instead.
pages.title: Advanced Tips

pages.text: $(l)Working with Forges$()$(br2)Metalworking creates intense heat. To survive:$(li)Remove all metal armor$(li)Stay wet if possible$(li)Work in short bursts$(li)Have water nearby to cool off$(li)Build in open, windy areas$(li)Consider nighttime smithing
